def verify_source_alias_addition(prior, before, current, context):
    from mediaingredientmech.ingredient_bundle_refresh import (
        SourceAliasAdditionContext,
        _form_member,
    )

    require(isinstance(context, SourceAliasAdditionContext), "typed context required")
    root = context.root
    require(root.absolute() == root.resolve(), "aliased root")
    require(content_sha256(current[MANIFEST]) == context.manifest_sha256, "manifest pin differs")
    require(_form_member(root, CODE).read_bytes() == _LOADED, "loaded verifier differs")
    old, new = read_json(before[MANIFEST]), read_json(current[MANIFEST])
    require(set(new) == set(old) | {UPDATE}, "manifest membership changed")
    mutable = {"artifacts", "source_owner_sha256", UPDATE}
    require(
        canonical_json({k: v for k, v in old.items() if k not in mutable})
        == canonical_json({k: v for k, v in new.items() if k not in mutable}),
        "retained policy history changed",
    )
    prefix = old.get(UPDATE, [])
    require(
        isinstance(prefix, list)
        and isinstance(new[UPDATE], list)
        and new[UPDATE][:-1] == prefix
        and len(new[UPDATE]) == len(prefix) + 1,
        "exactly one append required",
    )
    update = new[UPDATE][-1]
    require(
        set(update)
        == {
            "issue",
            "approval",
            "prior_manifest_sha256",
            "mapping_receipt",
            "mapping_receipt_sha256",
            "generation_manifest",
            "generation_manifest_sha256",
        },
        "unexpected update fields",
    )
    require(
        update["issue"] == ISSUE and update["approval"] == "NONE: scientific review is separate",
        "update confers approval or changes issue",
    )
    require(
        update["prior_manifest_sha256"] == content_sha256(before[MANIFEST]), "prior pin differs"
    )
    require(
        not {OWNER, NOTE_OWNER}.intersection(prior["record_inputs"]),
        "selected companion owner changed",
    )
    bound: dict[str, str] = {}

    def read(name):
        raw = _form_member(root, name).read_bytes()
        digest = content_sha256(raw)
        require(name not in bound or bound[name] == digest, "input changed during proof")
        bound[name] = digest
        return raw

    def historical(name):
        return subprocess.check_output(["git", "show", context.baseline + ":" + name], cwd=root)

    for path in (MANIFEST, SOURCE, SIDECAR, BASELINE):
        require(historical(path) == before[path], "durable baseline differs")
        require(read(path) == current[path], "current artifact differs")
    require(
        before[SIDECAR] == current[SIDECAR] and before[BASELINE] == current[BASELINE],
        "suppression sidecar/baseline changed",
    )
    for doc, values in ((old, before), (new, current)):
        require(
            doc["artifacts"] == {p: content_sha256(values[p]) for p in (SOURCE, SIDECAR, BASELINE)},
            "manifest artifact pins differ",
        )
    old_owner, new_owner = historical(OWNER), read(OWNER)
    verify_owner(old_owner, new_owner)
    require(old["source_owner_sha256"][OWNER] == content_sha256(old_owner), "old owner pin differs")
    expected_owners = dict(old["source_owner_sha256"])
    expected_owners[OWNER] = content_sha256(new_owner)
    note_before, note_after = historical(NOTE_OWNER), read(NOTE_OWNER)
    verify_provenance_owner(note_before, note_after)
    require(
        old["source_owner_sha256"][NOTE_OWNER] == content_sha256(note_before),
        "old note-owner pin differs",
    )
    expected_owners[NOTE_OWNER] = content_sha256(note_after)
    require(new["source_owner_sha256"] == expected_owners, "unaccounted owner inventory change")
    proof = verify_mapping_chain(root)
    require(receipt_inventory(root) == set(proof["receipt_paths"]), "receipt inventory differs")
    require(proof["receipt_paths"][-1] == update["mapping_receipt"], "not final native receipt")
    receipt_bytes = read(update["mapping_receipt"])
    require(
        content_sha256(receipt_bytes) == update["mapping_receipt_sha256"], "receipt pin differs"
    )
    receipt = proof["receipts"][-1]
    require(receipt == read_json(receipt_bytes), "replayed receipt differs")
    require(
        receipt["issue"] == ISSUE
        and receipt["before_sha256"] == content_sha256(before[SOURCE])
        and receipt["after_sha256"] == content_sha256(current[SOURCE]),
        "receipt endpoints differ",
    )
    require(
        len(receipt["records"]) == 2 and receipt["touched_subjects"] == [SUBJECT],
        "unexpected native owner scope",
    )
    owners = {r["source_record"]: r for r in receipt["records"]}
    require(set(owners) == {OWNER, NOTE_OWNER}, "unexpected native owner set")
    owner = owners[OWNER]
    require(
        owner["source_record"] == OWNER
        and owner["shape"] == "source_alias_addition"
        and owner["before_yaml_sha256"] == content_sha256(old_owner)
        and owner["after_yaml_sha256"] == content_sha256(new_owner),
        "native owner pins differ",
    )
    note = owners[NOTE_OWNER]
    require(
        note["shape"] == "source_provenance_note"
        and note["before_yaml_sha256"] == content_sha256(note_before)
        and note["after_yaml_sha256"] == content_sha256(note_after),
        "native note-owner pins differ",
    )
    require(len(receipt["changes"]) == 1, "expected one changed mapping")
    change = receipt["changes"][0]
    require(
        change["kind"] == "changed" and change["before_position"] == change["after_position"],
        "mapping membership or order changed",
    )
    require(
        receipt["position_map"] == list(range(1, len(receipt["position_map"]) + 1)),
        "mapping positions changed",
    )
    verify_row(change["before"], change["after"])
    event = yaml.safe_load(new_owner)["curation_history"][-1]
    require(
        change["after"]["mapping_date"] == event["timestamp"][:10], "row date differs from curation"
    )
    generation = read_json(read(update["generation_manifest"]))
    require(
        bound[update["generation_manifest"]] == update["generation_manifest_sha256"],
        "generation manifest pin differs",
    )
    # The generator's complete input/artifact inventory remains explicit evidence.
    # Attribution is hash-bound here; publication also checks the actual candidate row.
    require(
        generation["external_sssom_validation"] == "passed", "native generation did not validate"
    )
    for name, digest in proof["input_hashes"].items():
        require(content_sha256(read(name)) == digest, "replayed input changed")
    for name in (CODE, "src/mediaingredientmech/ingredient_bundle_refresh.py"):
        read(name)
    return {
        "scientific_approval_added": False,
        "baseline": context.baseline,
        "source_records": [OWNER, NOTE_OWNER],
        "appended_update": update,
        "receipt_paths": proof["receipt_paths"],
        "input_sha256": bound,
        "attribution_contract": "Native generation attribution hash-bound; full canonical and owner transition replayed.",
    }

"""How a mapping's quality becomes its SSSOM `confidence` and `mapping_justification`.

Two things can write these columns: MIM's own promotion helpers, and claw's
`build_mim_ingredient_sssom.py`, which regenerates the whole file. When they disagree,
whichever ran last wins and the columns flip back and forth across rebuilds with nothing
gating or reporting it -- measured on one promotion as 205 rows moving 0.99 -> 0.9, 49
moving 0.95 -> 0.99, and 189 justification flips, on a diff that otherwise showed zero
identity changes (#519).

**claw's rules are canonical here**, because claw is the generator: it rebuilds every row
from the records, so any value MIM writes that disagrees survives only until the next
build. Mirroring its rules is what makes a rebuild a no-op instead of a rewrite.

The two rules, and why they are what they are:

`SYNONYM_MATCH` is graded 0.99, not 0.95. MIM's schema glosses it "Matches known synonym
in ontology", which says how the term was *located*, not that the identity is
approximate -- `CLOSE_MATCH` is the value reserved for "semantically close but not
exact". A row found through an exact synonym is an exact identity claim, and it already
carries `skos:exactMatch`, so grading it below a label match contradicted its own
predicate.

Justification is derived, not asserted. A row found by string equality is
`semapv:LexicalMatching`; anything that needed a judgement is
`semapv:ManualMappingCuration`. MIM's writers used to hardcode the latter, which
described 107 records created by exact string matching as hand-curated.

Kept in step with claw by `tests/test_sssom_grading.py`, which reads claw's own constants
when the sibling checkout is present and skips when it is not -- the same shape as the
SSSOM validator's Rule B4.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from collections.abc import Callable

# Qualities that denote an exact identity, and so earn exact-match confidence.
EXACT_QUALITIES = frozenset({"EXACT_MATCH", "SYNONYM_MATCH"})

# Qualities reached by string equality rather than by a curator's judgement.
LEXICAL_QUALITIES = frozenset({"EXACT_MATCH", "LEXICAL_MATCH", ""})

CONFIDENCE_EXACT = "0.99"
CONFIDENCE_OTHER = "0.9"

JUSTIFICATION_LEXICAL = "semapv:LexicalMatching"
JUSTIFICATION_MANUAL = "semapv:ManualMappingCuration"

PREDICATE_EXACT = "skos:exactMatch"
PREDICATE_CLOSE = "skos:closeMatch"
#: A record graded NARROW_MATCH is *more specific* than its ontology term, so
#: under SKOS the term is the broader concept and the row is a ``broadMatch``:
#: ``A skos:broadMatch B`` asserts B is broader than A. MIM published
#: ``narrowMatch`` here until #390, which is the inverse -- ``skos:narrowMatch``
#: is a sub-property of ``skos:narrower``, so it asserted the ontology parent
#: was narrower than the MIM record. The grade name and the predicate agree
#: once the spec is applied: subject narrower <=> object broader.
PREDICATE_BROAD = "skos:broadMatch"


def confidence_for(quality: str | None) -> str:
    """SSSOM `confidence` for a record's `mapping_quality`."""
    return CONFIDENCE_EXACT if (quality or "") in EXACT_QUALITIES else CONFIDENCE_OTHER


def justification_for(quality: str | None) -> str:
    """SSSOM `mapping_justification` for a record's `mapping_quality`."""
    return JUSTIFICATION_LEXICAL if (quality or "") in LEXICAL_QUALITIES else JUSTIFICATION_MANUAL


def predicate_for(quality: str | None) -> str:
    """SSSOM `predicate_id` for a record's `mapping_quality`.

    Mirrors the builder: exact by default, `closeMatch` for any quality that is not an
    exact identity so downstream consumers do not read it as one, and `broadMatch` for
    NARROW_MATCH, where the MIM term is narrower than the ontology parent and the parent
    is therefore the broader concept (#390).

    Expressed as a rule rather than a table because the enumerated version covered five
    grades while the corpus uses nine -- PLACEHOLDER, CAS_RN_LOOKUP, LEXICAL_MATCH and
    BROAD_MATCH (339 records) raised KeyError on any write path that touched them (#525).
    """
    grade = quality or ""
    if grade == "NARROW_MATCH":
        return PREDICATE_BROAD
    if grade and grade not in EXACT_QUALITIES:
        return PREDICATE_CLOSE
    return PREDICATE_EXACT


# The grades the corpus uses today. Listed for documentation and for the tests, NOT as
# the set of permitted keys: `mapping_quality` is one of MIM's organically-growing enums
# (the validators treat it as warn-only), so any fixed list goes stale. An enumerated
# table already shipped this bug once -- `promote_microbedecoder_residual.py` knew three
# grades and raised KeyError on the rest -- and enumerating a longer list would only move
# the failure, not remove it. `PLACEHOLDER` (54 records) is the one an eleven-grade list
# missed.
KNOWN_QUALITIES = (
    "EXACT_MATCH",
    "SYNONYM_MATCH",
    "CLOSE_MATCH",
    "NARROW_MATCH",
    "BROAD_MATCH",
    "LEXICAL_MATCH",
    "CAS_RN_LOOKUP",
    "PLACEHOLDER",
    "MANUAL_CURATION",
    "LLM_ASSISTED",
    "PROVISIONAL",
    "FALLBACK_REGISTRY",
)


class _GradeTable(dict):
    """Dict view for writers that index by grade, total over every possible key.

    A KeyError here is a row that never gets written, which is strictly worse than a
    conservatively-graded one -- so an unrecognised grade falls back to the rule rather
    than raising. The rule fails low: anything not known to be an exact identity is
    graded below exact, so a new enum value cannot silently acquire exact-match
    confidence by being unknown.
    """

    def __init__(self, rule: Callable[[str | None], str]) -> None:
        super().__init__({quality: rule(quality) for quality in KNOWN_QUALITIES})
        self._rule = rule

    def __missing__(self, quality: str) -> str:
        return self._rule(quality)


CONFIDENCE = _GradeTable(confidence_for)
JUSTIFICATION = _GradeTable(justification_for)
PREDICATE = _GradeTable(predicate_for)

"""Data-derived metadata for emitted SSSOM mapping sets."""

from __future__ import annotations

import re
from collections.abc import Iterable, Mapping
from datetime import date
from typing import Any


def subset_date_metadata(
    metadata: Mapping[str, Any], rows: Iterable[Mapping[str, str]]
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Describe the emitted rows without inheriting an excluded row's date.

    Empty or wholly dateless sets omit both optional date fields; they have no
    row date to substantiate a version. Missing row dates stay untouched for
    Rule F to diagnose. Nonblank dates must be ASCII calendar dates, so malformed
    values cannot silently determine the set version. This adds no approval and
    does not modify row payloads, source provenance or other metadata (#1090).
    """
    dates = []
    for position, row in enumerate(rows, 1):
        raw = row.get("mapping_date", "")
        if not isinstance(raw, str):
            raise ValueError(f"Invalid mapping_date in emitted row {position}: {raw!r}")
        value = raw.strip()
        if not value:
            continue
        if not re.fullmatch(r"[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}", value):
            raise ValueError(f"Invalid mapping_date in emitted row {position}: {raw!r}")
        try:
            dates.append(date.fromisoformat(value))
        except ValueError as exc:
            raise ValueError(f"Invalid mapping_date in emitted row {position}: {raw!r}") from exc
    result = dict(metadata)
    if dates:
        newest = max(dates).isoformat()
        result.update(mapping_date=newest, mapping_set_version=newest)
    else:
        result.pop("mapping_date", None)
        result.pop("mapping_set_version", None)
    return result

    when = datetime.fromisoformat(event["timestamp"])
    require(
        when.utcoffset() == timedelta(0)
        and when >= datetime.fromisoformat(packet["evidence_not_before"]),
        "history predates evidence or is not UTC",
    )
    expected = deepcopy(before)
    for path in spec["delete"]:
        parts = path.split(".")
        parent = expected
        for key in parts[:-1]:
            require(isinstance(parent, dict) and key in parent, "missing deletion parent")
            parent = parent[key]
        require(isinstance(parent, dict) and parts[-1] in parent, "missing deletion field")
        del parent[parts[-1]]
    for path, value in spec["set"].items():
        parts = path.split(".")
        parent = expected
        for key in parts[:-1]:
            require(isinstance(parent, dict) and key in parent, "missing assignment parent")
            parent = parent[key]
        require(isinstance(parent, dict), "assignment parent is not a mapping")
        parent[parts[-1]] = deepcopy(value)
    expected["curation_history"].append(event)
    require(after == expected, "source changed outside reviewed matrix: " + name)
    return event


def expected_stock_source(record):
    """Native source vocabulary for this local registry row, without a KG suffix."""
    evidence = record["ontology_mapping"].get("evidence", [])
    sources = [
        f"MIM:{item['source'].strip()}" for item in evidence if item.get("source", "").strip()
    ]
    return "|".join(sources + ["MIM:curator=" + record["curation_history"][-1]["curator"]])


def verify_row_transition(before, current, receipt, event, source):
    """Only the exact stock CAS token and explicitly derived provenance may change."""
    headers = [
        [
            line
            for line in values[SSSOM_SOURCE].splitlines(keepends=True)
            if line.startswith(b"#")
            and not re.match(rb"# (mapping_date|mapping_set_version):", line)
        ]
        for values in (before, current)
    ]
    require(headers[0] == headers[1], "unrelated canonical header changed")
    _, old_columns, old_rows = _base_table(before[SSSOM_SOURCE])
    _, columns, rows = _base_table(current[SSSOM_SOURCE])
    require(
        old_columns == columns
        and len(old_rows) == len(rows)
        and receipt["position_map"] == list(range(1, len(rows) + 1))
        and receipt["changed_rows"] == 1
        and len(receipt["changes"]) == 1
        and receipt["added_rows"] == receipt["removed_rows"] == 0,
        "expected exactly one changed row with identity position map",
    )
    change = receipt["changes"][0]
    old, new = change["before"], change["after"]
    require(isinstance(old, dict) and isinstance(new, dict), "changed row endpoints absent")
    tokens = old["other"].split("|")
    require(tokens.count(CAS_TOKEN) == 1, "stock CAS token missing or duplicated")
    allowed = {"other", "source", "mapping_date", "validation_method"}
    require(
        old["subject_id"] == new["subject_id"] == SUBJECT
        and old["object_id"] == new["object_id"] == IDENTITY
        and old["predicate_id"] == new["predicate_id"] == "skos:exactMatch"
        and new["other"] == "|".join(token for token in tokens if token != CAS_TOKEN)
        and new["source"] == source
        and new["validation_method"] == ""
        and re.fullmatch(r"[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}", new["mapping_date"])
        and date.fromisoformat(new["mapping_date"])
        == datetime.fromisoformat(event["timestamp"]).date()
        and {k: v for k, v in old.items() if k not in allowed}
        == {k: v for k, v in new.items() if k not in allowed},
        "stock row exceeds exact CAS/provenance scope",
    )
    old_lines, new_lines = (
        [
            line
            for line in values[SSSOM_SOURCE].splitlines(keepends=True)
            if not line.startswith(b"#")
        ]
        for values in (before, current)
    )
    require(len(old_lines) == len(new_lines) == len(rows) + 1, "unexpected raw row layout")
    position = change["before_position"]
    require(position == change["after_position"], "changed row moved")
    require(
        all(
            a == b
            for i, (a, b) in enumerate(zip(old_lines, new_lines, strict=True))
            if i != position
        ),
        "unrelated canonical row bytes changed",
    )


def verify_stock_transition(prior, before, current, context, update, proof, historical, member):
    """Verify exact source shapes, immutable prefix and both historical-owner links."""
    root = context.root.resolve()
    require(
        update["issue"] == 268 and update["source_record"] == STOCK, "wrong issue or stock owner"
    )
    require(update["historical_owner_sha256"] == HISTORICAL_OWNER, "wrong historical stock pin")
    require(update["owner_before_sha256"] == ACTUAL_PREIMAGE, "wrong actual stock preimage")
    historical_paths = (
        subprocess.check_output(
            ["git", "ls-tree", "-r", "--name-only", context.baseline, "--", RECEIPTS_DIR], cwd=root
        )
        .decode()
        .splitlines()
    )
    prefix = {p for p in historical_paths if p.endswith(".json")}
    require(
        prefix == set(proof["receipt_paths"][:-1])
        and receipt_inventory(root) == prefix | {proof["receipt_paths"][-1]}
        and proof["receipt_paths"][-2] == BRIDGE,
        "historical receipt inventory is not the exact expected prefix",
    )
    inputs: dict[str, str] = {}

    def capture(name):
        raw = member(root, name).read_bytes()
        digest = content_sha256(raw)
        require(
            name not in inputs or inputs[name] == digest, "conflicting proof input hash: " + name
        )
        inputs[name] = digest
        return raw

    for name in sorted(prefix | set(HISTORICAL_CONTEXT) | set(FORM_REVIEWS)):
        require(capture(name) == historical(name), "historical receipt/FORM bytes changed: " + name)
    packet_raw = capture(PACKET)
    require(content_sha256(packet_raw) == PACKET_SHA256, "reviewed source packet changed")
    packet = read_json(packet_raw)
    for name, info in packet["files"].items():
        raw = capture(name)
        require(
            content_sha256(raw) == info["sha256"] and len(raw) == info["bytes"],
            "source capture changed",
        )
    owners = set(packet["owners"])
    require(len(owners) == 15 and STOCK in owners, "source owner scope differs")
    require(
        not owners.intersection(prior["record_inputs"]), "changed owner belongs to companion cohort"
    )
    receipt = proof["receipts"][-1]
    records = {r["source_record"]: r for r in receipt["records"]}
    require(
        set(records) == owners and len(receipt["records"]) == 15,
        "expected exactly fifteen source owners",
    )
    for name in sorted(owners):
        spec = packet["owners"][name]
        old_raw, raw = historical(name), capture(name)
        record = records[name]
        require(
            content_sha256(old_raw) == spec["before_yaml_sha256"] == record["before_yaml_sha256"]
            and old_raw == capture(spec["preimage"])
            and content_sha256(raw) == record["after_yaml_sha256"]
            and record["shape"] == spec["shape"],
            "actual owner endpoints/shape differ: " + name,
        )
        old, new = _load_yaml(old_raw.decode()), _load_yaml(raw.decode())
        event = verify_source_transition(name, old, new, packet)
        if name == STOCK:
            stock_event, stock_source = event, expected_stock_source(new)
    historical_link = record_supersession(
        proof,
        owner=STOCK,
        reviewed_sha256=HISTORICAL_OWNER,
        current_sha256=update["owner_after_sha256"],
    )
    suffix = record_supersession(
        proof,
        owner=STOCK,
        reviewed_sha256=ACTUAL_PREIMAGE,
        current_sha256=update["owner_after_sha256"],
    )
    require(
        historical_link is not None
        and suffix is not None
        and [r["path"] for r in historical_link["receipts"]] == [BRIDGE, proof["receipt_paths"][-1]]
        and [r["path"] for r in suffix["receipts"]] == [proof["receipt_paths"][-1]],
        "stock owner chain is not the exact historical bridge plus current suffix",
    )
    verify_row_transition(before, current, receipt, stock_event, stock_source)
    memberships = []
    for values in (before, current):
        decisions = [
            d
            for d in read_json(values[prior["base_review"]])["decisions"]
            if d["owner_record"] in owners
        ]
        require(
            len(decisions) == 27 and all(d["disposition"] == "WITHHOLD" for d in decisions),
            "all 27 scoped mappings must retain WITHHOLD",
        )
        memberships.append({(d["owner_record"], d["source_position"]) for d in decisions})
    require(memberships[0] == memberships[1], "affected mapping membership changed")
    for name in VERIFIERS:
        capture(name)
    require(member(root, VERIFIERS[0]).read_bytes() == _CODE, "loaded stock verifier differs")
    return {
        "owners": sorted(owners),
        "historical_receipt_count": len(prefix),
        "current_receipt_count": len(proof["receipt_paths"]),
        "form_reviews_byte_preserved": list(FORM_REVIEWS),
        "stock_historical_supersession": historical_link,
        "stock_actual_preimage_supersession": suffix,
        "policy_owner_map_contract": "Historical canonical inputs; only thiamine advances across two proved links.",
        "scientific_approval_added": False,
        "input_sha256": inputs,
    }

"""Chemical name normalization utilities for ontology matching.

This module provides functions to normalize chemical names by:
- Stripping hydrate notation (e.g., •7H2O, .2H2O)
- Removing catalog numbers (Fisher, Sigma, etc.)
- Fixing incomplete chemical formulas
- Expanding common abbreviations
- Generating search variants for ontology matching
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import re
from dataclasses import dataclass

# Hydrate notation patterns to strip
HYDRATE_PATTERNS = [
    r"[•·.]\s*\d+\s*H2O",  # •2H2O, .7H2O
    r"\s*\(hydrated\)",
    r"\s*(?<![a-z])(?:hemi|sesqui)?"
    r"(?:mono|di|tri|tetra|penta|hexa|hepta|octa|nona|deca|dodeca)?hydrate\b",
]

# Catalog/CAS patterns to strip
CATALOG_PATTERNS = [
    r"\s*\(Fisher [^)]+\)",
    r"\s*\(Sigma [^)]+\)",
    r"\s*\(CAS:\s*[^)]+\)",
    r"\s*\(MCIB [^)]+\)",
    r"\s*\([A-Z]{2,5}[- ][\w-]+\)",  # Generic catalog (XX NNNN)
]

# Common chemical formula abbreviations → full names
FORMULA_TO_NAME = {
    "NaCl": "sodium chloride",
    "KCl": "potassium chloride",
    "MgSO4": "magnesium sulfate",
    "MgCl2": "magnesium chloride",
    "CaCl2": "calcium chloride",
    "CaSO4": "calcium sulfate",
    "K2HPO4": "dipotassium phosphate",
    "KH2PO4": "monopotassium phosphate",
    "NaHCO3": "sodium bicarbonate",
    "Na2CO3": "sodium carbonate",
    "FeSO4": "ferrous sulfate",
    "FeCl3": "ferric chloride",
    "MnCl2": "manganese chloride",
    "ZnSO4": "zinc sulfate",
    "CuSO4": "copper sulfate",
    "NH4Cl": "ammonium chloride",
    "NaNO3": "sodium nitrate",
    "KNO3": "potassium nitrate",
    "H3BO3": "boric acid",
    # Gases and water. Anaerobic recipes name these constantly -- `N2 gas` (71 recipe
    # mentions) and `Oxygen gas` (42) head the unresolved residual -- and their formulas
    # share almost no characters with their ontology labels, so without an entry here no
    # search variant and no string-similarity measure will ever connect `N2` to
    # `dinitrogen`. The names are the CHEBI labels, so the variant lands on the term.
    "N2": "dinitrogen",
    "O2": "dioxygen",
    "H2": "dihydrogen",
    "CO2": "carbon dioxide",
    "CO": "carbon monoxide",
    "CH4": "methane",
    "H2S": "hydrogen sulfide",
    "NH3": "ammonia",
    "H2O": "water",
    "N2O": "dinitrogen oxide",
    "SO2": "sulfur dioxide",
}

# Common abbreviations → full terms
ABBREVIATION_EXPANSIONS = {
    "dH2O": "distilled water",
    "H2O": "water",
    "EDTA": "ethylenediaminetetraacetic acid",
    "Tris": "tris(hydroxymethyl)aminomethane",
    "MES": "2-(N-morpholino)ethanesulfonic acid",
    "HEPES": "4-(2-hydroxyethyl)-1-piperazineethanesulfonic acid",
}

# Common incomplete formulas → corrected versions
FORMULA_CORRECTIONS = {
    "K2HPO": "K2HPO4",
    "KH2PO": "KH2PO4",
    "NaNO": "NaNO3",
    "MgCO": "MgCO3",
    "CaCO": "CaCO3",
    "Na2SiO": "Na2SiO3",
}


@dataclass
class NormalizationResult:
    """Result of normalizing a chemical name."""

    original: str
    normalized: str
    variants: list[str]
    applied_rules: list[str]


def strip_hydrate_notation(name: str) -> tuple[str, bool]:
    """Remove hydrate notation from chemical name.

    Examples:
        MgSO4•7H2O → MgSO4
        CaCl2.2H2O → CaCl2
        sodium chloride hydrate → sodium chloride

    Returns:
        Tuple of (cleaned_name, was_modified)
    """
    original = name
    for pattern in HYDRATE_PATTERNS:
        name = re.sub(pattern, "", name, flags=re.IGNORECASE)
    return name.strip(), name != original


def strip_catalog_info(name: str) -> tuple[str, bool]:
    """Remove catalog numbers and supplier codes.

    Examples:
        NaCl (Fisher S271-500) → NaCl
        MgSO4 (Sigma 230391) → MgSO4
        KCl (CAS: 7447-40-7) → KCl

    Returns:
        Tuple of (cleaned_name, was_modified)
    """
    original = name
    for pattern in CATALOG_PATTERNS:
        name = re.sub(pattern, "", name)
    return name.strip(), name != original


def fix_incomplete_formula(name: str) -> tuple[str, bool]:
    """Correct common incomplete chemical formulas.

    Examples:
        K2HPO → K2HPO4
        NaNO → NaNO3

    Returns:
        Tuple of (corrected_name, was_modified)
    """
    stripped = name.strip()
    for incomplete, complete in FORMULA_CORRECTIONS.items():
        if stripped == incomplete or stripped.startswith(incomplete + " "):
            corrected = name.replace(incomplete, complete, 1)
            return corrected, True
    return name, False


def expand_abbreviation(name: str) -> str | None:
    """Expand common chemical abbreviations to full names.

    Examples:
        dH2O → distilled water
        EDTA → ethylenediaminetetraacetic acid

    Returns:
        Expanded name if abbreviation recognized, else None
    """
    stripped = name.strip()
    return ABBREVIATION_EXPANSIONS.get(stripped)


def formula_to_common_name(formula: str) -> str | None:
    """Convert chemical formula to common name.

    Examples:
        NaCl → sodium chloride
        MgSO4 → magnesium sulfate

    Returns:
        Common name if formula recognized, else None
    """
    stripped = formula.strip()
    return FORMULA_TO_NAME.get(stripped)


def normalize_chemical_name(name: str) -> NormalizationResult:
    """Apply all normalization rules to a chemical name.

    This is the main entry point for normalization. It applies all
    applicable rules and tracks which ones were used.

    Args:
        name: Original chemical name to normalize

    Returns:
        NormalizationResult with normalized name, variants, and applied rules
    """
    applied_rules = []
    current = name

    # Step 1: Strip catalog info
    current, modified = strip_catalog_info(current)
    if modified:
        applied_rules.append("stripped_catalog")

    # Step 2: Strip hydrate notation
    current, modified = strip_hydrate_notation(current)
    if modified:
        applied_rules.append("stripped_hydrate")

    # Step 3: Fix incomplete formulas
    current, modified = fix_incomplete_formula(current)
    if modified:
        applied_rules.append("fixed_incomplete_formula")

    normalized = current.strip()

    # Generate search variants
    variants = generate_search_variants(normalized, name)

    return NormalizationResult(
        original=name,
        normalized=normalized,
        variants=variants,
        applied_rules=applied_rules,
    )


def generate_search_variants(normalized: str, original: str) -> list[str]:
    """Generate multiple search variants for ontology matching.

    Creates various forms of the chemical name to try when searching
    ontologies, ordered from most specific to most general.

    Args:
        normalized: The normalized chemical name
        original: The original (un-normalized) name

    Returns:
        List of search variant strings (duplicates removed)
    """
    variants = []

    # Original name (in case normalization was too aggressive)
    if original.strip():
        variants.append(original.strip())

    # Normalized name (catalog/hydrate stripped)
    if normalized and normalized != original.strip():
        variants.append(normalized)

    # Try without hydrate if not already done
    no_hydrate, _ = strip_hydrate_notation(original)
    if no_hydrate and no_hydrate not in variants:
        variants.append(no_hydrate)

    # Try formula → common name expansion
    common_name = formula_to_common_name(normalized)
    if common_name:
        variants.append(common_name)

    # Try abbreviation expansion
    expanded = expand_abbreviation(normalized)
    if expanded:
        variants.append(expanded)

    # Try with incomplete formula fixed
    fixed, _ = fix_incomplete_formula(normalized)
    if fixed and fixed not in variants:
        variants.append(fixed)
        # Also try common name of fixed formula
        fixed_common = formula_to_common_name(fixed)
        if fixed_common:
            variants.append(fixed_common)

    # Remove duplicates while preserving order
    seen = set()
    unique_variants = []
    for v in variants:
        v_lower = v.lower()
        if v_lower not in seen:
            seen.add(v_lower)
            unique_variants.append(v)

    return unique_variants


def categorize_unmapped_name(name: str) -> str:
    """Categorize an unmapped ingredient name.

    Returns one of:
    - SIMPLE_CHEMICAL: Likely a simple chemical with notation issues
    - COMPLEX_MIXTURE: Vitamin solution, metal solution, media mixture
    - ENVIRONMENTAL: Soil, seawater, etc.
    - INCOMPLETE: Generic or unclear term
    - PLACEHOLDER: Reference to external source
    - UNKNOWN: Cannot categorize
    """
    name_lower = name.lower()

    # Placeholders
    if any(
        phrase in name_lower
        for phrase in [
            "full composition",
            "see source",
            "available at",
            "composition available",
        ]
    ):
        return "PLACEHOLDER"

    # Complex mixtures (but exclude if just a chemical with "solution" descriptor)
    complex_keywords = [
        "vitamin",
        "trace metal",
        "supplement",
        "mixture",
        "medium",
        "media",
    ]
    if any(phrase in name_lower for phrase in complex_keywords):
        return "COMPLEX_MIXTURE"

    # Single chemical in solution form (e.g., "Thiamine HCl solution")
    # Still treat as simple chemical if just one compound
    if "solution" in name_lower:
        # Check if it's a simple chemical solution vs complex mixture
        words = name.split()
        if len(words) <= 3:  # e.g., "CaCl2 solution"
            return "SIMPLE_CHEMICAL"
        return "COMPLEX_MIXTURE"

    # Environmental samples
    if any(
        phrase in name_lower
        for phrase in [
            "soil",
            "seawater",
            "sea water",
            "creek",
            "sediment",
            "greenhouse",
        ]
    ):
        return "ENVIRONMENTAL"

    # Incomplete/generic terms
    generic_terms = [
        "vitamin b",
        "trace element",
        "mineral",
    ]
    if any(phrase in name_lower for phrase in generic_terms) and len(name.split()) <= 2:
        return "INCOMPLETE"

    # Natural salt is incomplete
    if "natural" in name_lower and "salt" in name_lower:
        return "INCOMPLETE"

    # Check if looks like chemical formula or name with catalog/hydrate
    has_formula_pattern = bool(re.search(r"[A-Z][a-z]?\d*[A-Z]", name))  # e.g., NaCl, MgSO4
    has_simple_formula = bool(re.search(r"^[A-Z][a-z]?[A-Z0-9]+", name))  # Starts with element
    has_catalog = bool(re.search(r"\([A-Z][a-z]+ [A-Z0-9-]+\)", name))
    has_hydrate = bool(re.search(r"[•·.]\s*\d+\s*H2O", name))

    if has_formula_pattern or has_simple_formula or has_catalog or has_hydrate:
        return "SIMPLE_CHEMICAL"

    # Check if it's in our known formulas
    stripped = name.strip()
    if stripped in FORMULA_TO_NAME or stripped in FORMULA_CORRECTIONS:
        return "SIMPLE_CHEMICAL"

    # Check if ends with common salt forms
    if re.search(r"(chloride|sulfate|nitrate|phosphate|carbonate)$", name_lower):
        return "SIMPLE_CHEMICAL"

    # Default
    return "UNKNOWN"

"""Client for retrieving chemical properties from ChEBI and PubChem APIs."""

from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
import json
import logging
import math
import re
import time
from dataclasses import dataclass
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from pathlib import Path
from urllib.parse import quote

import requests

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

# Cache directory for chemical properties
CACHE_DIR = Path.home() / ".cache" / "mediaingredientmech" / "chemical_properties"

# API endpoints
CHEBI_OLS_API = "https://www.ebi.ac.uk/ols4/api/ontologies/chebi/terms"
PUBCHEM_API = "https://pubchem.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/rest/pug/compound"

# Rate limiting (5 requests per second)
MIN_REQUEST_INTERVAL = 0.2
_last_request_time = 0.0


@dataclass
class ChemicalProperties:
    """Chemical structure and properties for a chemical entity."""

    molecular_formula: str | None = None
    smiles: str | None = None
    inchi: str | None = None
    molecular_weight: float | None = None
    data_source: str | None = None
    retrieval_date: str | None = None

    def to_dict(self) -> dict[str, str | float]:
        """Convert to dictionary for YAML serialization."""
        result: dict[str, str | float] = {}
        if self.molecular_formula:
            result["molecular_formula"] = self.molecular_formula
        if self.smiles:
            result["smiles"] = self.smiles
        if self.inchi:
            result["inchi"] = self.inchi
        if self.molecular_weight is not None:
            result["molecular_weight"] = self.molecular_weight
        if self.data_source:
            result["data_source"] = self.data_source
        if self.retrieval_date:
            result["retrieval_date"] = self.retrieval_date
        return result


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class OlsChemicalProperties:
    """An exact OLS retrieval and immutable schema-safe property snapshot.

    This establishes source consistency, not the identity of an ingredient.
    Record-aware callers must still compare the declared substance and form.
    ``to_dict`` returns a new block; legacy mutable/cache properties are never
    embedded in this envelope.
    """

    ontology_id: str
    returned_ontology_id: str
    label: str
    synonyms: tuple[str, ...]
    source_url: str
    retrieved_at: str
    response_sha256: str
    property_values: tuple[tuple[str, str | float], ...]

    def to_dict(self) -> dict[str, str | float]:
        """Return a fresh properties block without adding envelope-only slots."""
        return dict(self.property_values)


def _unique_json_object(pairs: list[tuple[str, object]]) -> dict[str, object]:
    """Reject duplicate JSON keys instead of silently replacing source evidence."""
    result: dict[str, object] = {}
    for key, value in pairs:
        if key in result:
            raise ValueError("Duplicate OLS JSON key")
        result[key] = value
    return result


def _ols_annotation_value(annotation: dict, *keys: str, numeric: bool = False):
    """Read one agreed value across current/legacy keys; never choose the first.

    Recognized keys, when present, must contain nonempty lists. Text values
    may differ only in surrounding whitespace; masses must be finite positive
    numbers. Repeated identical values are allowed, conflicting values refuse.
    """
    values: set[str | float] = set()
    for key in keys:
        if key not in annotation:
            continue
        raw_values = annotation[key]
        if not isinstance(raw_values, list) or not raw_values:
            raise ValueError("Malformed OLS annotation")
        for value in raw_values:
            if numeric:
                if isinstance(value, bool) or not isinstance(value, (str, int, float)):
                    raise ValueError("Malformed OLS mass")
                parsed = float(value)
                if not math.isfinite(parsed) or parsed <= 0:
                    raise ValueError("Invalid OLS mass")
                values.add(parsed)
            else:
                if not isinstance(value, str) or not value.strip():
                    raise ValueError("Malformed OLS text annotation")
                values.add(value.strip())
    if len(values) > 1:
        raise ValueError("Conflicting OLS annotation values")
    return next(iter(values)) if values else None


class ChemicalPropertiesClient:
    """Retrieve chemical properties from ChEBI and PubChem APIs."""

    def __init__(self, cache_enabled: bool = True):
        """Initialize the client.

        Args:
            cache_enabled: Whether to use file-based caching.
        """
        self.cache_enabled = cache_enabled

    def get_ols_properties(self, ontology_id: str) -> OlsChemicalProperties | None:
        """Retrieve one exact defining ChEBI term, without cache or PubChem.

        The body hashed is the same byte stream parsed. Missing/conflicting
        term identity, obsolete/imported terms, malformed recognized annotation
        fields and ambiguous values refuse. This does not infer ingredient or
        hydrate identity; callers must apply record/form consistency guards.
        Transport/HTTP errors propagate as ``requests.RequestException`` so
        record-aware callers can distinguish provider failures from refusals.
        """
        if not isinstance(ontology_id, str) or not re.fullmatch(r"CHEBI:[1-9][0-9]*", ontology_id):
            return None
        iri = f"http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/CHEBI_{ontology_id.split(':')[1]}"
        url = f"{CHEBI_OLS_API}/{quote(quote(iri, safe=''), safe='')}"
        try:
            self._rate_limit()
            response = requests.get(url, timeout=10, allow_redirects=False)
            response.raise_for_status()
            if response.status_code != 200:
                return None
            raw = response.content
            if not isinstance(raw, bytes):
                return None
            data = json.loads(raw, object_pairs_hook=_unique_json_object)
            if not isinstance(data, dict):
                return None
            if (
                data.get("obo_id") != ontology_id
                or data.get("iri") != iri
                or data.get("ontology_name") != "chebi"
                or data.get("is_defining_ontology") is not True
                or data.get("is_obsolete") is not False
                or data.get("ontology_prefix", "CHEBI") != "CHEBI"
                or data.get("short_form", ontology_id.replace(":", "_"))
                != ontology_id.replace(":", "_")
                or data.get("term_replaced_by") is not None
            ):
                return None
            label = data.get("label")
            annotation = data.get("annotation")
            synonyms = data.get("synonyms", [])
            if not isinstance(label, str) or not label.strip() or not isinstance(annotation, dict):
                return None
            if not isinstance(synonyms, list) or any(
                not isinstance(value, str) or not value.strip() for value in synonyms
            ):
                return None
            if "id" in annotation and _ols_annotation_value(annotation, "id") != ontology_id:
                return None
            formula = _ols_annotation_value(
                annotation, "generalized_empirical_formula", "formula", "has_molecular_formula"
            )
            smiles = _ols_annotation_value(annotation, "smiles_string", "smiles", "SMILES")
            inchi = _ols_annotation_value(annotation, "inchi_string", "inchi", "InChI")
            mass = _ols_annotation_value(annotation, "mass", numeric=True)
            if not any(value is not None for value in (formula, smiles, inchi, mass)):
                return None
            retrieved_at = datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()
            properties = ChemicalProperties(
                molecular_formula=formula,
                smiles=smiles,
                inchi=inchi,
                molecular_weight=mass,
                data_source=f"ChEBI {ontology_id}; {url}",
                retrieval_date=retrieved_at,
            )
            return OlsChemicalProperties(
                ontology_id=ontology_id,
                returned_ontology_id=data["obo_id"],
                label=label.strip(),
                synonyms=tuple(dict.fromkeys(value.strip() for value in synonyms)),
                source_url=url,
                retrieved_at=retrieved_at,
                response_sha256=hashlib.sha256(raw).hexdigest(),
                property_values=tuple(properties.to_dict().items()),
            )
        except (ValueError, TypeError, OverflowError) as exc:
            logger.warning("Strict OLS properties refused for %s: %s", ontology_id, exc)
            return None

    def get_properties(
        self,
        ontology_id: str,
        label: str,
        source: str,
    ) -> ChemicalProperties | None:
        """Get chemical properties for an ontology term.

        Args:
            ontology_id: Ontology ID in CURIE format (e.g., CHEBI:26710).
            label: Human-readable label for the term.
            source: Ontology source (CHEBI, FOODON, etc.).

        Returns:
            ChemicalProperties if available, None otherwise.
        """
        # Only process CHEBI terms
        if source != "CHEBI":
            logger.debug("Skipping non-CHEBI term: %s (%s)", ontology_id, source)
            return None

        # Check cache first
        if self.cache_enabled:
            cached = self._get_from_cache(ontology_id)
            if cached is not None:
                return cached

        # Extract CHEBI numeric ID
        chebi_id = ontology_id.split(":")[-1]

        # Try to get properties from ChEBI OLS API
        props = self._get_chebi_properties(chebi_id, ontology_id)

        # If we have ChEBI ID, try to enrich with PubChem SMILES/InChI
        if props and chebi_id:
            pubchem_props = self._get_pubchem_properties(chebi_id)
            if pubchem_props:
                # Merge PubChem data
                if pubchem_props.smiles and not props.smiles:
                    props.smiles = pubchem_props.smiles
                if pubchem_props.inchi and not props.inchi:
                    props.inchi = pubchem_props.inchi
                if pubchem_props.molecular_weight and not props.molecular_weight:
                    props.molecular_weight = pubchem_props.molecular_weight
                # Update source to indicate both
                if props.data_source == "ChEBI":
                    props.data_source = "ChEBI+PubChem"

        # Cache the result
        if props and self.cache_enabled:
            self._save_to_cache(ontology_id, props)

        return props

    def _get_chebi_properties(self, chebi_id: str, ontology_id: str) -> ChemicalProperties | None:
        """Retrieve properties from ChEBI OLS API v4.

        Args:
            chebi_id: Numeric ChEBI ID (e.g., 26710).
            ontology_id: Full ontology ID (e.g., CHEBI:26710).

        Returns:
            ChemicalProperties with formula and molecular weight if available.
        """
        try:
            # OLS4 requires the IRI to be double-URL-encoded so that the
            # server's path-decoding step leaves a still-encoded IRI for the
            # downstream lookup. Single-encoding yields 400 from the API.
            iri = f"http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/CHEBI_{chebi_id}"
            encoded_iri = quote(quote(iri, safe=""), safe="")
            url = f"{CHEBI_OLS_API}/{encoded_iri}"

            # Rate limiting
            self._rate_limit()

            response = requests.get(url, timeout=10)
            response.raise_for_status()

            data = response.json()

            # Extract annotation fields. OLS4 renamed the chemical-property keys —
            # formula -> generalized_empirical_formula, and SMILES/InChI are now
            # *_string (smiles_string / inchi_string) — and dropped the legacy
            # `formula` key entirely, which silently broke formula/SMILES/InChI
            # enrichment. Read the current names first, falling back to the legacy
            # ones for resilience. (Abstract classes / polymers carry none of these,
            # which is the expected "no formula" ceiling, not a failure.)
            annotation = data.get("annotation", {})

            def _first(*keys):
                for k in keys:
                    vals = annotation.get(k)
                    if vals:
                        return vals[0]
                return None

            formula = _first("generalized_empirical_formula", "formula", "has_molecular_formula")
            smiles = _first("smiles_string", "smiles", "SMILES")
            inchi = _first("inchi_string", "inchi", "InChI")
            molecular_weight = None
            mass = _first("mass")
            if mass is not None:
                try:
                    molecular_weight = float(mass)
                except (ValueError, TypeError):
                    pass

            if formula or smiles or inchi or molecular_weight:
                return ChemicalProperties(
                    molecular_formula=formula,
                    smiles=smiles,
                    inchi=inchi,
                    molecular_weight=molecular_weight,
                    data_source="ChEBI",
                    retrieval_date=datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(),
                )

            logger.debug("No chemical properties found in ChEBI for %s", ontology_id)
            return None

        except requests.RequestException as e:
            logger.warning("Failed to fetch ChEBI properties for %s: %s", ontology_id, e)
            return None
        except (KeyError, ValueError, TypeError) as e:
            logger.warning("Error parsing ChEBI response for %s: %s", ontology_id, e)
            return None

    def _get_pubchem_properties(self, chebi_id: str) -> ChemicalProperties | None:
        """Retrieve SMILES and InChI from PubChem using ChEBI cross-reference.

        Args:
            chebi_id: Numeric ChEBI ID.

        Returns:
            ChemicalProperties with SMILES and InChI if available.
        """
        try:
            # Search PubChem by ChEBI ID
            search_url = f"{PUBCHEM_API}/name/CHEBI:{chebi_id}/cids/JSON"

            # Rate limiting
            self._rate_limit()

            search_response = requests.get(search_url, timeout=10)

            # PubChem returns 404 if not found - this is normal
            if search_response.status_code == 404:
                logger.debug("No PubChem entry found for CHEBI:%s", chebi_id)
                return None

            search_response.raise_for_status()
            cids_data = search_response.json()

            cids = cids_data.get("IdentifierList", {}).get("CID", [])
            if not cids:
                logger.debug("No PubChem CIDs found for CHEBI:%s", chebi_id)
                return None

            # Use the first CID
            cid = cids[0]

            # Get properties for this CID
            props_url = (
                f"{PUBCHEM_API}/cid/{cid}/property/" f"CanonicalSMILES,InChI,MolecularWeight/JSON"
            )

            # Rate limiting
            self._rate_limit()

            props_response = requests.get(props_url, timeout=10)
            props_response.raise_for_status()
            props_data = props_response.json()

            properties = props_data.get("PropertyTable", {}).get("Properties", [])
            if not properties:
                return None

            prop = properties[0]
            smiles = prop.get("CanonicalSMILES")
            inchi = prop.get("InChI")
            mol_weight = prop.get("MolecularWeight")

            if smiles or inchi:
                return ChemicalProperties(
                    smiles=smiles,
                    inchi=inchi,
                    molecular_weight=float(mol_weight) if mol_weight else None,
                    data_source="PubChem",
                    retrieval_date=datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(),
                )

            return None

        except requests.RequestException as e:
            # Don't log 404s as warnings - they're expected for many ChEBI terms.
            #
            # `hasattr(e, "response")` is always True: requests sets `.response`
            # on every RequestException and leaves it None for errors that never
            # got a reply (connection reset, DNS, timeout). Reading
            # `.status_code` off that None raised inside the handler, so a single
            # transient network blip aborted the whole enrichment batch instead
            # of skipping one record.
            response = getattr(e, "response", None)
            if response is None or response.status_code != 404:
                logger.debug("Failed to fetch PubChem properties for CHEBI:%s: %s", chebi_id, e)
            return None
        except (KeyError, ValueError, TypeError) as e:
            logger.warning("Error parsing PubChem response for CHEBI:%s: %s", chebi_id, e)
            return None

    def _rate_limit(self):
        """Enforce rate limiting (5 requests per second)."""
        global _last_request_time
        now = time.time()
        elapsed = now - _last_request_time
        if elapsed < MIN_REQUEST_INTERVAL:
            time.sleep(MIN_REQUEST_INTERVAL - elapsed)
        _last_request_time = time.time()

    def _get_cache_path(self, ontology_id: str) -> Path:
        """Get cache file path for an ontology ID."""
        # Use sanitized ontology ID as filename
        safe_id = ontology_id.replace(":", "_")
        return CACHE_DIR / f"{safe_id}.json"

    def _get_from_cache(self, ontology_id: str) -> ChemicalProperties | None:
        """Retrieve properties from cache if available."""
        cache_path = self._get_cache_path(ontology_id)
        if not cache_path.exists():
            return None

        try:
            with open(cache_path) as f:
                data = json.load(f)
            return ChemicalProperties(
                molecular_formula=data.get("molecular_formula"),
                smiles=data.get("smiles"),
                inchi=data.get("inchi"),
                molecular_weight=data.get("molecular_weight"),
                data_source=data.get("data_source"),
                retrieval_date=data.get("retrieval_date"),
            )
        except (OSError, json.JSONDecodeError) as e:
            logger.warning("Failed to read cache for %s: %s", ontology_id, e)
            return None

    def _save_to_cache(self, ontology_id: str, props: ChemicalProperties):
        """Save properties to cache."""
        cache_path = self._get_cache_path(ontology_id)
        try:
            cache_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
            with open(cache_path, "w") as f:
                json.dump(props.to_dict(), f, indent=2)
        except OSError as e:
            logger.warning("Failed to save cache for %s: %s", ontology_id, e)

    """Normalize exact source labels without making broad lexical guesses."""
